q: If det A ≠ 0, then Ax = b has…
why: A is invertible, so x = A⁻¹b is the one and only solution.

q: If det A = 0, then Ax = b has…
o: either no solution or infinitely many
why: Like parallel lines (none) or the same line twice (infinitely many). Which one depends on b.

q: Solve Ax = b using the inverse.
why: Multiply on the left: A⁻¹Ax = A⁻¹b, so x = A⁻¹b. With matrices the order matters.

q: For matrices, x = b/A is fine.
why: Myth. Matrices can't be divided. Use A⁻¹, when it exists.

q: A system with more equations than unknowns has no solution.
why: Usually it has none, but the extra equations can agree with the others, for example when one equation is repeated.
